1.2.1.6-f3.text: Ex Pituitosis pituitosi, ex biliosis biliosi, ex lienosis & melancholicis, melancholici

translations.literal: From phlegmatic [parents] phlegmatic [children], from choleric choleric, from splenetic and melancholic, melancholic.
translations.note: The sidenote backs up Burton's claim in the main text that melancholy is a hereditary disease. The thought is close to Hippocrates' argument in On the Sacred Disease that phlegmatic parents have phlegmatic children, bilious parents bilious children, and splenetic parents splenetic children. The Hippocratic list as I know it does not include the melancholic, so this looks like Burton's own adaptation.
translations.text: From the phlegmatic come the phlegmatic, from the choleric the choleric, from the splenetic and melancholic the melancholic.

translations.note: Adjectives used as nouns for parents and offspring. Burton gives no rendering of this line nearby; the main text at the note only argues that melancholy is hereditary.
translations.text: From the phlegmatic come phlegmatic children, from the choleric choleric, from the splenetic and melancholic melancholic.
